name: Extrait de parfum

lead: Extrait de parfum, often just called parfum or extrait, is the highest concentration tier in perfumery. Wikipedia lists it at roughly 15 to 30 percent aromatic compounds by volume, compared with about 5 to 15 percent for eau de toilette, and a typical wear time of around 6 to 8 hours.[1]

For looks, it works through scent rather than appearance: people use fragrance as part of grooming so that they are remembered as well-kept and attractive up close. A concentrated format gives a smaller amount a longer presence on skin, which is why fragrance enthusiasts reach for it when they want a scent to last through a day or evening.

paras: Extraits are typically applied sparingly to pulse points or clothing, since a small amount carries. Many are sold in small bottles, and some are poured rather than sprayed. Wear time varies by composition and skin, and the labels extrait, eau de parfum and eau de toilette are not standardized, so one brand's eau de parfum can be stronger than another's extrait.[1]

Fragrance ingredients are a common cause of contact dermatitis and allergic reactions, and higher concentrations increase exposure per application. Concentration names are imprecise across brands.[1] Price is typically higher per bottle than lighter formats, though a bottle is used in small amounts.

angle.text: A fragrance is applied to skin or clothing so that the wearer smells pleasant to people nearby. Extraits are chosen when a longer-lasting scent is wanted from a small number of applications.

lead: Extrait de parfum, also sold as parfum or pure perfume, is the highest concentration of fragrance oil in a perfume, generally 15 to 30 percent aromatic compounds by volume, with about 20 percent commonly cited as typical.[1] Because there is less alcohol, many extraits feel richer and sit closer to the skin than lighter formats.

People include fragrance in grooming to leave a pleasant impression, and a more concentrated format is chosen for longevity: Wikipedia gives roughly 6 to 8 hours for parfum against 2 to 4 hours for eau de toilette, though the same page notes that concentration labels vary between houses.[1]
infobox: Eau de parfum, eau de toilette, eau de cologne[1]

paras: Perfumes are sold in tiers defined by how much aromatic material is dissolved in alcohol or oil. Wikipedia lists parfum or extrait at 15 to 30 percent, eau de parfum at about 15 to 20 percent, eau de toilette at 5 to 15 percent and eau de cologne at 2 to 3 percent.[1]

The page stresses that these names are imprecise: an eau de toilette from one house can be more concentrated than an eau de parfum from another, and the same name can be used for formulas that differ between concentrations.[1]

Fragrance is part of a grooming routine alongside skin care, haircuts and clothing. Extraits are favored by enthusiasts who want a scent to last across a long day or evening with few applications, because higher oil content generally means a stronger and longer-lasting scent.[1]

According to Wikipedia, perfume price depends on extraction method, labor, difficulty and quality of ingredients; natural materials are often but not always costlier, and synthetic aromatics are generally cheaper though some have long syntheses.[1]
